scene_breakdown.narration: Welcome back to IDE Guide! Today we are taking an objective look at Cursor AI. Quick disclaimer before we start: IDE Guide is completely independent and not sponsored by any editor developer. All opinions are strictly objective.

scene_breakdown.flow_prompt: Dynamic screen recording overlay with glowing highlighted code lines in Cursor AI. Cinematic camera drift across developer desk with code flowing.
scene_breakdown.narration: Cursor AI is categorized as a AI-Native Code Editor. Here are the top reasons developers choose it: Deep repository-wide indexing for instant context-aware code generation; Native AI chat, inline edits (Cmd+K), and multi-file auto-refactoring; Forked from VS Code, ensuring 100% extension compatibility; Fast Claude 3.5 Sonnet & GPT-4o integration

scene_breakdown.flow_prompt: Minimalist UI illustration showing performance meters, RAM consumption, and feature gaps highlighted in subtle amber red.
scene_breakdown.narration: However, no editor is perfect. Here are the main drawbacks you need to know: Requires active internet connection for advanced AI features; Privacy concerns for enterprise codebases without enterprise plan; Free tier request limits exhaust quickly on active coding days
